scenes.title: 6:15 AM Bedroom Snooze Trap & Kitchen Counter Coffee Spill
scenes.era: Modern adult bedroom & sunlit-adjacent morning kitchen

layout.description: Warm suburban adult bedroom with a twin-bell brass analog alarm clock on an oak nightstand beside a rumpled linen duvet, leading directly to an espresso kettle counter.

positions.who: Groggy 46-year-old commuter (stylized 2.5D vinyl character in rumpled heather-gray cotton pajama top)
positions.where: reaching a heavy arm out from under the linen duvet toward the vibrating brass nightstand alarm clock
positions.facing: angled sideways toward the oak nightstand

positions.who: Awake household partner / clinical sleep observer (stylized 2.5D vinyl character in crisp olive morning robe holding a ceramic mug)
positions.where: standing in the bedroom doorway watching the third consecutive alarm slap
positions.facing: toward the bed and nightstand clock

props.name: Twin-bell brushed-brass mechanical alarm clock with top plunger snooze bar
props.period_detail: classic tactile analog clock face with physical vibrating hammer bells and zero digital screen text
props.physical_behavior: State A brass bells shudder violently at 6:15 AM -> State B heavy palm slams the top brass snooze plunger flat down while head drops back into the pillow

props.name: Gooseneck stainless pour-over kettle and ceramic morning coffee mug
props.period_detail: matte-black gooseneck kettle steaming over a white stoneware mug on oak counter
props.physical_behavior: State A sleep-fogged hand tilts steaming kettle two inches off-center -> State B hot dark coffee splashes onto the oak saucer rim beside the mug

actions.verb_sequence: slams palm onto the vibrating brass alarm plunger -> staggers upright into the kitchen five minutes later and pours steaming coffee onto the counter rim beside the mug

reactions.reaction: catches the tilting kettle handle and slides the alarm clock across the room toward the bright window

scenes.wardrobe: Heather-gray cotton pajama shirt and flannel trousers; partner in olive morning robe.
scenes.lighting: Dim slate-blue dawn bedroom shadow contrasting with warm kitchen task light.
scenes.recognition_hook: Your hand can slap the alarm and walk to the kettle in ten seconds—while the decision-maker behind your forehead is still fast asleep!

key_visual.description: a groggy adult reaching out from a rumpled duvet to slam a vibrating brass mechanical alarm clock plunger before pouring morning coffee beside the mug

scenes.title: Outdoor Sunlit Front-Porch Steps: Flushing Morning Sleep Inertia With Daylight
scenes.era: Modern 6:45 AM sunlit residential front porch and tree-lined sidewalk

layout.description: Open-air residential front stoop and sunlit tree-lined sidewalk bathed in crisp golden morning sunshine.

positions.who: Refreshed 46-year-old adult commuter (in navy quarter-zip sweater)
positions.where: stepping outdoors onto the sunlit front porch stairs holding a warm ceramic mug and breathing crisp morning air
positions.facing: into the golden eastern morning sun

props.name: Front-door brass handle and steaming stoneware mug in outdoor sunlight
props.period_detail: solid brass latch opening wide onto sunlit neighborhood trees
props.physical_behavior: hand swings the front door wide open into bright morning sun and posture straightens crisply

actions.verb_sequence: rises on a single alarm across the room -> swings open the front porch door into bright outdoor sunlight and takes a brisk sidewalk walk

reactions.reaction: blinks once in golden daylight as posture and gaze sharpen with alert clarity

scenes.wardrobe: Navy quarter-zip knit over collared shirt.
scenes.recognition_hook: Stepping straight into outdoor morning sun helps flush lingering delta fog out of your prefrontal cortex.

scenes.title: Neuroimaging Wake Suite: 5-Minute Delta Fog vs 25-Minute Prefrontal Reboot
scenes.era: 2019 Lyon & Walter Reed neuroimaging sleep laboratory

layout.description: High-key clinical sleep-scanner room with a cushioned scanner bed, scalp sensor cap, and physical handheld reaction clicker.

positions.where: volunteer seated up on scanner couch clicking a dual-button thumb responder while researcher checks a wall clock at 5 vs 25 minutes

props.name: Handheld mechanical thumb clicker and wall sweep-second timer
props.period_detail: clean clinical reaction-speed button and analog wall timer
props.physical_behavior: hesitant slow thumb clicks at minute 5 transform into crisp rapid clicks by minute 25

actions.verb_sequence: fumbles slow thumb presses 5 minutes after deep-sleep waking -> clicks crisply and accurately 25 minutes post-awakening

reactions.reaction: records the sharp 25-minute prefrontal recovery curve

scenes.wardrobe: Volunteer in soft clinical scrub top; researcher in white lab coat.
scenes.recognition_hook: Waking straight out of deep slow-wave sleep floods daytime brain networks with delta waves for nearly half an hour.
